requirements.text: Students should be able to search the library catalog and check real-time availability of materials.
Students should be able to borrow, return, and renew items online.
Students should be able to book study rooms online, selecting date, time, and capacity.
Students should be able to view their current loans, due dates, reservation history, and outstanding fines.
Students should receive automated email reminders for due dates and fines.
Staff should have an inventory management system that allows easy addition, updating, and retiring of catalog items.
Staff should have access to detailed usage reports providing insights on loan volumes, popular items, study room utilization, and fine revenue.
Librarians should be able to place holds or restrictions on student accounts based on fine thresholds.
The system must integrate with the existing student record system to verify enrollment status for borrowing and booking.
Access to relevant student information must include full name, student ID, and enrollment status.
The system must comply with GDPR, ensuring lawful and transparent data collection and processing.
Sensitive data must be stored securely, with access limited to authorized staff only.
The system must have mechanisms for students to view their own data and request corrections.
There must be clear policies on data retention and deletion.
Integration with the existing student record system must be thoroughly tested to ensure seamless data flow.
Budget considerations must be taken into account for both implementation and ongoing maintenance.
Staff training must be provided to ensure comfort with the new system.
The timeline for data migration must be meticulously planned to avoid data loss and ensure accurate transfer.
